stories.detail: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, the team announced Thursday. Hurts was listed as a full participant in Friday's practice before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday's game in London. The Eagles released a statement detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot. "On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf," the team said. "He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report. "Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. stories.summary: The special teams gunner is set to make his debut with Seattle.
stories.detail: Through the first month of the season, the Seattle Seahawks struggled with kickoff coverage and rank near the bottom of the league in yards allowed per return, but they’re set to gain a key special teams asset ahead of a crucial Week 6 road matchup against the Denver Broncos. The team announced they’ve elevated wide receiver and special teams gunner Irv Charles, as well as linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo from the practice squad. Both will make their team debuts. Acquired from the New York Jets in May , Charles missed the first five games while on injured reserve with a knee issue but was designated to return to practice on October 7. Seattle activated him to the active roster on Tuesday , although, he was released a day later to make room for running back Velus Jones Jr . As a vested veteran, Charles wasn’t subject to waivers and rerouted to the practice squad. Upon his return, Charles is expected to play a key role on kick and punt returns—areas where he’s highly regarded. On the defensive side, Ciarlo’s elevation was expected given the Seahawks will be without starting linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) and Chazz Surratt (chest), leaving a thin group even thinner. stories.title: Aaron Rodgers vs. Todd Bowles should be quite a chess match when Steelers visit the Buccaneers
stories.summary: — Todd Bowles will have to be quite creative to surprise Aaron Rodgers.
stories.detail: TAMPA, Fla. -- — Todd Bowles will have to be quite creative to surprise Aaron Rodgers . Known for his complex defensive schemes and disguising his blitz packages, Bowles and his Tampa Bay Buccaneers are facing an elite quarterback who has seen everything in a distinguished NFL career. Rodgers just passed Peyton Manning to move into third place for most career passing touchdowns, including the postseason. It’ll be quite the chess match when Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers (3-2) face off against the Buccaneers (1-4) on Sunday. “Obviously, Todd has a history of bringing a lot of pressures,” Rodgers said. “We’ll be ready for those. But he brings a lot of stuff you haven’t seen before, so, good disguise team, good pressure team. We’ll have to pick them up and get the ball out.” The 42-year-old Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, has thrown three TD passes in three straight games. But he’s 1-2 against Bowles’ Tampa Bay defenses, including a loss in the 2020 NFC championship game. Rodgers threw for 442 yards and two touchdowns and ran for two scores against Bowles and the Jets in a 44-38 overtime victory with Green Bay in 2018. “It’s a nightmare game-planning against him,” Bowles said. “He…

stories.title: Glorious Seahawks vs. Broncos throwback uniform showdown is NFL's best this season
stories.summary: The Seahawks vs. Broncos "Thursday Night Football" throwback showdown leads columnist Nate Davis' list of the Top 10 NFL uniform matchups of 2026.
stories.detail: Rest assured, when you log in for Thursday night’s game between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on Amazon Prime, you’re in the right place – not getting high-definition NFL Films clips of John Elway trying to beat Kenny Easley in coverage. But what could be the best game of Week 6 of the 2026 season is certainly going to have a retro vibe calling back the 1970s, ‘80s and 90s, when the Broncos and Seahawks were AFC West rivals. That’s because both clubs will be donning glorious throwback uniforms – vintage looks a good subset of both fan bases would like to see restored as these teams’ primary looks. (This is probably a good time to remind them neither team won a Super Bowl in these classic threads, but details, details.) The pleasing visual will probably serve – definitely serve in this football fashionista’s opinion – as this season’s top uniform matchup. And, lest you take issue with my Elway-Easley scene setter, yes, Denver’s throwbacks are technically a callback to the pre-Elway 1977 team , the first in Broncos history to reach the Super Bowl (they were blown out by the Dallas Cowboys in Super Bowl 12 ). stories.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor not fretting slower start than usual
stories.summary: Taylor may have lower numbers than usual, but he's still in the top 10 in rushing yards and rushing TDs.
stories.detail: INDIANAPOLIS -- The true indication of a player's greatness might be what kind of reaction comes when they produce average performances. Take Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor , for instance. He appeared for his scheduled media gathering with local reporters on Thursday, and the conversation quickly turned to the lack of the explosive plays for which he has become famous. "Explosive runs?" Taylor said. "You talking about the 40-, 50-yard touchdowns? "Everybody loves those." Taylor then pointed out that he registered a 20-yard run in last Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of his longest of the season. A fair point, but the retort might have had more impact if Taylor hadn't had two runs of 80 yards or longer just last season. The whole exchange was a good reminder of the lofty standards Taylor is held to. It's why his current 3.9-yard-per-rush average is somewhat alarming for a player who has averaged 4.8 yards per carry in his career. It's why his third-down conversion rate of 33.3% is noticeable, considering his career mark is 47.3%. And, perhaps more than anything, it's why it's so remarkable that Taylor hasn't posted a 100-yard rushing performance in 1…

teamStories.detail: HENDERSON, Nev. -- Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty , who has been battling ankle and foot injuries, said he's feeling "great" ahead of Sunday's home game against the Buffalo Bills . "I'm ready to go," Jeanty said. Added coach Klint Kubiak: "He's playing." Jeanty was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, and Kubiak said he was "excited" about giving his running back more reps in practice. Jeanty's status for last week's game against the New England Patriots was in question after he missed practice last Friday due to a flare-up of plantar fasciitis, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. He worked out pregame to determine whether he was good enough to play. Jeanty, who has not been 100% healthy since sustaining an ankle sprain in late August, had his worst rushing performance of the season in the 45-17 road loss, totaling 27 yards on 10 carries. In the last four games, Jeanty has averaged 47.3 yards per game. Despite Jeanty's struggles, he is hoping for a breakout performance at some point. stories.title: Maxey: Healthy Embiid 'changes everything' for Sixers
stories.summary: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.
stories.detail: CAMDEN, N.J. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers. Embiid's 10-year career has been marred by injury. He has never played a full 82 games and has played more than 60 games just four times in his career. Over his 10 seasons, he has averaged just 49 games per season, which doesn't include him missing his first two seasons with injury.​ Embiid played just 38 games last season, double his number from 2024, as he navigated right hip complications, left knee management and appendicitis. The injuries have often kept Embiid out of training camp and the preseason -- crucial time for a team to get comfortable playing with a player like Embiid, the 2023 NBA MVP. "You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow." Maxey said his experience gives him the advantage. He knows where Embiid likes to catch the ball, where he wants guards to cut and other tendencies that he has learned over six years of playing together. In less than a week, the Knicks will raise their long-awaited third championship banner on national television at Madison Square Garden. It’s a day 53 years in the making. teamStories.detail: Prior to the NFL season, I published an article on the preseason NFL power ranking for all 32 teams on Yahoo Sports. In that article, I explained how to use a ratings system to help price spreads, how to use it to action bets and what potential pitfalls in the process exist. I highly recommend reading that article to also lay the foundation for my NBA power ratings below. Instead of retooling the same concepts into NBA terms, I am going to provide my ratings and then note which teams I see as potential risers and fallers once the NBA regular season action begins. These are currently built off of using NBA regular season win totals, title odds to differentiate teams with the same win total number, current state of injury news, and the first few regular season games we have priced. I then add some manual adjustment. The only major difference to note in using these instead of NFL is the change in home-court rating from 1.5 to 3 points from a neutral site. teamStories.title: Victor Wembanyama, Spurs dominate annual NBA GM survey
teamStories.summary: An annual survey of NBA general managers projects the Spurs to win the NBA title this season, with Victor Wembanyama earning MVP and Defensive Player of the Year honors.
teamStories.detail: An annual survey of NBA general managers revealed Thursday that the league is bracing for a full takeover by Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs . After winning 62 games and making a surprise trip to the NBA Finals last season, the Spurs emerged as the survey's 2027 championship favorite, and Wembanyama was projected to win MVP and be selected as the league's best defensive player. In addition, the 7-foot-4 French center received 93% of the votes in response to the question: "If you were starting a franchise today and could sign any player in the NBA, who would it be?" The general managers did not view the Spurs as overwhelming title favorites. San Antonio received 50% of the votes, narrowly topping the 2025 champion Oklahoma City Thunder . The defending champion New York Knicks , who were picked to win the Eastern Conference, and the new-look Philadelphia 76ers , bolstered by LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , also received votes to win the title. Wembanyama, 22, was selected as the heavy favorite to win his first MVP award with 77% of the votes. Denver 's Nikola Jokic (10%) and Minnesota 's Anthony Edwards (7%) also earned nods.
